decks.name: Open Flame / Открытое пламя
decks.speed: Fast aggro/tempo; lethal clock around turn 5-6, purely on unpreventable damage.
decks.strategy: Mono-red burn that wins by inevitable damage, not by owning the board. Cheap RR bodies with bypass/pierce push face through any blocker; incandescence auras turn the whole team into an anemone of extra attack; a reach package (spark from crystals, sear on-death, direct burn spells) closes 6-10 damage independent of what is on the table. self_lifesteal/cauterize buy the extra turn a race needs.
decks.wincon: Reduce the enemy hero to 0 through damage the opponent cannot block or absorb: bypass/pierce combat + incandescence multiplier, plus spark activations, sear on-death, and burn spells from hand.
decks.hero: Пирр / Pyrrhus — passive Feverlight: the first creature you play each turn costs 1 less generic (min 0).
decks.gameplan: T1: drop a 1-pip enabler and start chipping face — Cinder Moth (bypass) or Lance Gnat (pierce), or Blood Impling for a lifesteal body vs other aggro; Ember Whelp banks a guaranteed sear even if it trades. T2: an RR commitment body (Ash Courser bypass / Stinging Hornet pierce) plus, on a spare beat, Blood Dawn for +1 team attack; Feverlight discounts the turn's first creature. T3: Feverlight shaves an RR+1 threat to RR — Blast Beetle (sear 2), Spark Gunner (spark 2), or Bonfire Polyp / War Drums to crank incandescence to +2 or +3 across the board; start spending leftover crystals on spark pings. T4: keep the beats coming with Ember Cannon (durable spark), holding Fire Spit to blow up the one blocker that actually matters or just sending it face. T5-6: assemble reach for the kill — Pyrrhus' Wrath (5 face), Sear Comet (4 face), Flame Titan (5/5 bypass that also sears on death), plus crystal-fed spark and any sear from trades. The board can be behind; the hero still dies.
decks.curve_note: Mono-red with no ramp, so power comes from color commitment, not mana growth: nearly every real threat is RR and every capstone is RRR — literally uncastable in a rainbow pile. By mana (counting spells/auras): 10 at 1, 12 at 2, 12 at 3, 4 at 4, 2 at 5. Aggressive but top-complete because the top end is reach, not fat bodies. Feverlight trims the first creature each turn (RR+1 to RR, RR+2 to RR+1) to keep tempo without any ramp card. 20 unique cards, all x2, summing to exactly 40.
decks.matchups: Most beats: Green (Overgrowth) and Blue (Glass Hour) — bypass/pierce and the reach package ignore their blockers and race their ramp/spell setup before it pays off; GB (Floodtide) and GV (Evergreen) — the clock kills before their midrange/combo loop assembles, and burn to face doesn't care about their value engine. Most loses to: Yellow (Long Noon) — provoke/shield/ward walls plus blind and lifegain blunt combat and out-heal the burn; RG (Rot and Bloom) — lifedrain + Requiem out-sustains the race turn for turn; YG (Bastion) — Bulwark armor, regen and go-tall lifegain outlast the reach total. Mirror/other red is a coin-flip decided by whoever curves the bypass bodies first.

decks.name: Long Noon / Долгий полдень
decks.speed: Slow control / lock — never races, stabilizes by turn 4-5 then drips out the kill
decks.strategy: A wall of light. Cheap provoke bodies backed by shield/ward/firststrike absorb the aggro turns for free, blind and flare switch off the one attacker that matters, and a deep healing package (regen ticks, the Витраж aura, the hero passive, cauterize walls, direct hero-heal) keeps everything alive. That same healing is the offense: Reflux converts every heal event into face damage, so surviving IS attacking. Bulwark stacks hero armor to make the wall literally unkillable, and awakened strobe finishers swing into the face twice to close.
decks.hero: Гелия / Helia — passive Dawnlight: at start of your turn, heal your most-wounded creature +1 HP. (This heal routes through the normal heal path, so with a Reflux body out it also pings the enemy face.)
decks.gameplan: T1: drop Марево (0/3 provoke+shield) or Проблеск (1/2 firststrike+regen) to blunt the first attacker for free. T2: Веха / Оберег / Клинок зари to stack provoke walls, or Затмение to blind their best attacker for 2 turns; regen and Dawnlight begin ticking. T3: land the engine — Венец (Reflux 1) or Столп света (cauterize wall) plus the Витраж aura; Полдень mass-blinds a wide board. T4: Оплот зари starts stacking hero armor (Bulwark 2) while Гаснущий свет / Гелиодор hold the line; hero is now healing 2-3 times a turn, each ping going face through Reflux. T5: Солнцеворот (Reflux 2) or Зенит (strobe wall) — every heal now drips 2-3 to face. T6+: Гелиос swings twice and Затмение полдня locks their whole board with blind 3 + a 6 heal (a Reflux burst). You have stabilized; the drip is inevitable.
decks.wincon: Inevitability via Reflux. Corona (Reflux 1) and Solstice (Reflux 2) turn the deck's heavy, unavoidable healing — regen ticks, the Витраж aura, Dawnlight, cauterize combat, the Lull/Total Eclipse hero-heals — into recurring face damage the opponent cannot interact with. It is closed out by an awakened strobe wall (Зенит / Гелиос) attacking the hero twice. The deck does not race; it out-survives, then drips.
decks.curve_note: 20 unique cards, exactly 2 copies each = 40. Curve is front-loaded for survival: 1-drop x2, 2-drop x5, 3-drop x5, 4-drop x4, 5-drop x2, 6-drop x2. Nine cards carry a YY pip and three carry YYY, so the walls and payoffs are hard-committed mono-Yellow (uncastable as a splash) while the single-Y bodies/removal are the cheap glue — a mono deck leaning RR/RRR-equivalent as required. Known weakness baked in: Yellow has no card draw and no hard removal, so the deck runs 2-ofs of every impactful body and answers threats by disabling (blind), not killing.
decks.matchups: MOST BEATS — Open Flame (Red aggro): provoke walls + shield/ward/firststrike eat their attack steps for zero cards, regen/cauterize/Dawnlight/Lull heal past the burn faster than they deal it, blind switches off their bypass/pierce threat, and Reflux races their own face damage back at them. Long Noon simply outlives the clock. False Light (Violet go-wide illusions): Полдень and Затмение полдня mass-blind the whole board so the wide army can't attack at all; provoke forces what can attack into firststrike walls; flare blinds on death; 1-HP illusions do nothing to armored, healing walls while the Reflux drip finishes. MOST LOSES — Overgrowth (Green ramp-bombs): ramp lands resonance/growth titans that go over the walls; with no hard removal, blind only stalls one bomb a turn and provoke just feeds a trampling body — they outscale the drip. Arc Light (Red/Blue combo-loop): pinpoint/reach spell burn and Echo+birefringence bursts hit the face THROUGH shields and around provoke, killing faster than Reflux drips and ignoring the whole wall. Evergreen (Green/Violet loop): stealth evades provoke and mirage/renewal recursion grinds through temporary blind — they go around the lock instead of breaking it.

decks.name: Overgrowth / Буйный рост
decks.strategy: Solo-ramp: light -> crystals -> body. Spend the first turns turning tempo into permanent crystals and cheap walls, then drop a single overcost bomb that no removal in the format can trade with, and close before aggro would have.
decks.hero: Флора / Flora — passive Verdant: при 6+ кристаллах первый потраченный за ход кристалл возвращается (refund 1 mana each turn once you hit the ramp threshold, letting you cast a capstone AND a protection/pump spell in the same turn).
decks.wincon: One unanswerable oversized body — a resonance Heartwood (10-14/14), an undergrowth Colossus, or a growth Titan/Worldroot — that outclasses every removal in the roster; or a Forest's Waking anthem alpha strike across a germinate/spores-flooded board. Verdant makes these land a full turn early.
decks.gameplan: T1-2: Primrose / Crystal Mole / Springlight — bank permanent crystals and put down a 0/4 wall vs early pressure. T3: Sower (germinate fodder) or Strangleveil to fight a key threat; Sunwell if unpressured to jump ahead. T4-5: land Elder Oak (mulch keeps the board healthy), Grove Warden and Thornwall (growth bodies that snowball each upkeep), Bounty Tree to push past 6 crystals and switch on Verdant. T6-7: capstone turn — Heartwood comes down as a 10-14/14 off crystal count, or Undergrowth Colossus / Ancient Titan; Verdant's refund lets you also hold up Wild Growth to save it from a fight. T7-8: Worldroot (10/10 growing) or Forest's Waking +2/+2 anthem for the lethal overrun. Everbloom recurs your best bomb if the first one is answered, so the over-the-top plan has a second copy built in.
decks.curve_note: Bell curve peaking at 4-5 with a deliberate ramp tail: 4 two-drops, 8 three-drops, 10 four-drops, 10 five-drops, then 8 cards at 6-8. Twelve of the cheap slots ramp or block, funding the 8 top-end payoffs. The thin two-drop count (only 4) is the intended aggro weakness. Heavy GG/GGG pips on every payoff and capstone make the deck uncastable as a rainbow splash and reward the mono commitment.
decks.matchups: MOST BEATS — Long Noon (Yellow control/lock): goes over the top; a resonance/growth bomb exceeds their point removal and is too big to profitably blind, and Verdant refund out-values their disable tempo. Glass Hour (Blue control/spells): growing bodies outpace freeze/counter — they cannot answer a fresh 14/14 every turn, and Everbloom re-buys the threat through their removal. Rot and Bloom (RG attrition-drain): our capstones are simply bigger than their sacrifice-value engine; we go tall above their board and their drain clock is too slow to race our ramp. MOST LOSES — Open Flame (Red aggro): we durdle on ramp while they burn face; 4 two-drops and germinate fodder can't stabilize before sear/spark reach closes. Arc Light (RB aggro/combo): fast clock plus pinpoint reach punches through our walls before turn 6-7. Still Shroud (YV control/lock): blind + refract + stealth locks or unmakes our single big threat — the eggs-in-one-basket capstone plan gets disabled. Floodtide (GB tempo): scatter/freeze bounce our bombs for tempo blowouts while they ramp and pressure at once.

decks.name: Стеклянный час / Glass Hour
decks.colors: Blue (mono) — leans BB/BBB commitment on payoffs, single-pip glue for early reactivity
decks.hero: Кьяра / Chiara — passive Clairvoyance (владелец постоянно видит верхнюю карту своей колоды)
decks.strategy: Reactive tempo-control: freeze/scatter/chill hold the board, scry+draw and haze win the resource war, then close with Echo prowess bodies and a birefringence+pinpoint burst.
decks.wincon: Grind card advantage while the board stays frozen, then close two ways: (1) Echo prowess bodies (Shimmer Refractor, Facet Oracle) balloon as you chain cheap spells in one turn; (2) the birefringence (Mirror Ray / Double Vision) + pinpoint (Sharp Spread) unabsorbable double-hit clears the last blocker and Deep Leviathan / Hoarfrost Colossus provide inevitability under a full board-freeze (Ice Tomb / Deep Freeze).
decks.gameplan: T1-2: hold up Frost Grip / Undertow, drop Focal Drake or Glacier Wall to eat the first attacker; Clairvoyance lets you sequence scry perfectly. T2-3: Farsight to pull ahead on cards, Cold Snap vs aggro or Haze Veil vs spell decks; Frost Sentinel / Ebb Spirit trade up or bounce a key blocker. T3-4: land an Echo body (Facet Oracle, then Shimmer Refractor on BB), start freezing the biggest threats with Frost Grip / Slow Frost. T4-5: Deep Freeze or Ice Tomb locks the whole board; Winter Stream refills. T5-6: alpha turn — chain 2-3 cheap spells to pump Shimmer Refractor +4/+6, Mirror Ray makes Sharp Spread (pinpoint) hit two targets unabsorbably, Deep Leviathan freezes their board on entry and swings for the close.
decks.curve_note: 1-drops (8): Frost Grip, Undertow, Focal Drake, Double Vision. 2 (10): Frost Sentinel, Glacier Wall, Ebb Spirit, Farsight, Haze Veil. 3 (10): Facet Oracle, Mirror Ray, Sharp Spread, Slow Frost, Cold Snap. 4 (4): Shimmer Refractor, Deep Freeze. 5 (4): Winter Stream, Ice Tomb. 6 (4): Hoarfrost Colossus, Deep Leviathan. BB/BBB commitment is top-loaded onto every payoff; twelve single-pip cards keep the early game reactive and mono-castable.

decks.name: False Light / Ложный свет
decks.hero: Эреб / Erebos — passive "Lighteater / Пожиратель света": any creature that deals combat damage to your hero permanently loses 1 attack (min 0). Protects the fragile swarm by punishing every attacker that races back.
decks.speed: Medium — evasive chip clock online turns 2-4, go-wide alpha turns 5-6
decks.strategy: Go-wide evasive swarm of half-real bodies. Stealth + glimmer give an unpunishable chip clock the opponent cannot target or profitably block; split/haunt/mirage flood illusions that fuel undergrowth on real bodies; refract + Erebos protect the fragile threats; decoy/awaken hide threats in the mana row and refill after removal.
decks.wincon: Overwhelm: a wide board (illusions + stealth bodies) with undergrowth-pumped real bodies that the opponent (board cap 8) cannot fully block; alpha with False Dawn for lethal. Stealth/refract blank targeted removal, glimmer chips 2-4 past blockers every turn, decoy/awaken re-deploy so removal never fully clears.
decks.gameplan: T1-2: land cheap evasive bodies (Dim Ember, Unseen Prowler) and a glimmer aura (Dusk Moth / Glimmer Lantern) so one creature enters untargetable each turn; bank The Returned as crystals or set Hidden Blade/Sleeping Threat behind decoy in the mana row where the opponent cannot see them. T3-4: seed the swarm with split (Halflight, Twin Shade, Haunting Double) and Mirage Swarm / Fractured Whisper to flood illusions; spend Waning Light / Unmaking on their key blocker or provoke-wall; glimmer keeps a safe 2-4 chip going. T4-5: drop undergrowth payoffs (False Marshal, Mirage Sovereign) that balloon off the illusion count, with refract making the real bodies removal-proof; decoy threats wake free from the mana row for a surprise body. T5-6: alpha with False Dawn (+2/+1 team) across a board the opponent cannot fully block; Erebos shrinks anything that swings back, haunt leaves copies, awaken/decoy refill the grind.

decks.name: Rot and Bloom / Тлен и всходы
decks.speed: Grindy midrange attrition; natural kill turns 6-8, explosive Wake burst possible turn 5-6. Wins from an empty board.
decks.strategy: Aristocrats. The deck does not win by combat — it wins by its own creatures DYING. Green makes cheap, self-replacing fodder (spores/germinate/Renewal); Red converts each death into reach and lifegain. Every friendly death is worth 3-5 face damage once the engine is online: sear pings directly, the hero passive heals 1 which fires Reflux for more face, and Requiem adds a second point-of-damage + heal that ALSO re-triggers Reflux. Sac outlets (harvest, Sacrificial Sheaf, Wake) let you convert fodder into damage on demand, so blockers and board-locks do not stop the clock.
decks.hero: Гумус / Humus — passive loam / Перегной: whenever a friendly creature dies, your hero gains +1 HP. (This heal also triggers any Reflux you control, so every death is at least "heal 1 + Reflux ping" for free.)
decks.gameplan: T1: drop fodder — Spark Tick (R, dies for 1 face) or Rot Cap (G, dies into a Sprout). T2: Carrion Scarab / Resin Shoot (bank a crystal for germinate) / Ash Moth; start trading fodder into their board — each trade fires spores + sear + hero-heal. T3: land an engine piece — Blood Bramble (drains and grows off deaths), Blood Acolyte (heal->face), Spore Shepherd (crystal->Sprout), Bloatcap (0/4 wall vs aggro that later bursts into 3 Sprouts), or Cinder Boar. T4: the pivot turn — Barrow Mourner (Requiem 2) or Crimson Surge (Reflux 2 aura) or Field Reaper (repeatable sac outlet); now every friendly death = 2 face + heal + Reflux ping. T5+: Ash Eater top-end; Gorging Slug is huge off accumulated deaths. Close: either grind the drain loop (sac fodder via harvest/Sacrificial Sheaf/combat -> hero heals -> Reflux -> Requiem face+heal -> Reflux again), or slam Wake on a wide Sprout board for 2 face per creature as a burst finish. Sacrificial Sheaf refuels the hand mid-grind by turning a spent body into 2 cards.
decks.wincon: Incremental drain: each friendly death is converted to unblockable face damage (sear + Requiem + Reflux-via-hero-heal) while topping your hero off, so the attrition race is unwinnable for the opponent. Wake is the burst kill — sacrifice the whole Sprout board for 2 face each. All damage is death-gated and ignores blockers, so the deck kills even from an empty board or through a board-lock.
decks.curve_note: 4 / 12 / 12 / 10 / 2 across 1-2-3-4-5 mana. Deliberately fodder-dense at 1-3 (deaths are the resource), five payoff/capstone 4-drops, one 5-drop top-end. Crystals from Resin Shoot fuel germinate, but the deck also functions with zero ramp — germinate is a bonus outlet, not a dependency.

decks.hero: Tiziana / Тициана — passive Palette: the first multicolour (2+ colour) card you play each turn, draw a card. Every RB card in the list refuels the combo.
decks.speed: Fast (aggro-combo); clock turns 1-3, burst kill turns 5-6.
decks.strategy: Cheap prowess bodies (echo) turn every refraction into extra damage; a chain of cheap spells simultaneously pumps the board and throws reach at the face, doubled by birefringence and pushed through walls by pinpoint. The deck kills from an empty-looking board.

Pinpoint carries the last points through Shield/Ward.
decks.gameplan: T1: mono-pip glue — Storm Firefly, or Double Vision to pre-load the engine, or a reactive Frost Grip. T2: drop a multicolour body (Volt Swift / Volt Eel / Arc Mantis) — Palette draws off the first RB card, start chipping; bypass on Volt Swift ignores blockers. T3: Twin Hornet / Ember Oracle / Storm Tyrant, and begin short 1-spell chains to trade up (Jolt/Cold Shatter/Crimson Rift kill a blocker while pumping prowess). T4: Sharp Contrast swings a race, or keep sculpting the hand with Farsight; hold burn. T5-6 (kill turn): with the board down, empty the hand — every spell adds +1/+0 to each echo body AND points to the face; birefringence doubles a bolt, Spark Gunner/Ember Cannon convert leftover crystals, Thunderhead reads the whole chain, and pinpoint punches the final damage through walls. The deck punishes any opponent who spent turns 1-4 setting up instead of pressuring.

decks.colors: Green/Violet (GV) — mono-green ramp/fodder enablers, mono-violet illusion enablers, and GGV/GVV heavy-splash bombs that enforce both colours.
decks.curve_note: 20 unique cards, every one a 2-of = exactly 40. Deliberately light on 1-drops (only Mossy Acolyte x2) — under Gemma you would rather bank turn 1 for a crystal than commit a fragile body into Red. Bulk sits at 2 and 3 mana (ten cards each) for early fodder, ramp and the aristocrat/recursion shells. A dense 4-cost tier (12 cards: Fen Cultivator, Echo Fawn, Mirror Garden, Second Sowing, Bramble Ox, Dusk Hunter) is the engine floor, made reliably castable by photosynthesis ramp (Mossy Acolyte, Fen Cultivator) and Facet banking. Only three 5+ cards (Crystal Colossus GGV, Sprawling Wisp GVV at 5; Dormant Rampart GGV at 6) as finishers — you rarely hard-cast them off curve, you ramp or wake into them.
decks.gameplan: Mulligan for a 2-mana ramp/fodder piece (Mossy Acolyte, Sprout Warden, Humus Beetle) plus both a green and a violet source. T1: Mossy Acolyte, or bank a spare bomb for a crystal (Gemma reclaims it later, buffed). T2: Sprout Warden / Humus Beetle / Compost Bed start the fodder-and-aristocrat shell; or Dim Phantom for evasive chip. T3: Spore Mother or Splintered Effigy flood the board, Barrow Ivy brings the Renewal loop online, or Grove Skirmish answers a key blocker. T4 is the engine turn: Fen Cultivator ramps into fives, Echo Fawn / Mirror Garden copy a growing body, Second Sowing bulk-refills from the graveyard. T5-6: land Crystal Colossus (scales with every crystal you banked) or Sprawling Wisp (scales with your wide illusion board), protect it with Veil of Glints (glimmer) or hide behind sprouts, then mirage it for a second giant at 1HP. From here the loop is self-sustaining: every friendly death — sprouts, illusions, chumps, bombs — triggers compost (grow Humus Beetle/Bramble Ox), Renewal/reclaim (card back to hand) and haunt (leave a 1HP copy), so you manufacture threats faster than the opponent can remove them. Gemma's Facet ties it together: bank surplus bombs as mana early, then wake them later at +1/+1, turning ramp fuel back into buffed bodies and letting Dormant Rampart / Dusk Hunter appear off-curve.
decks.wincon: Attrition inevitability: out-card and out-body the opponent through the Renewal + haunt + compost + reclaim recursion web (their resources deplete, yours loop back), then close with resonance/undergrowth capstones and their mirage copies going both tall and wide. You do not race — you make the long game unlosable on cards.
decks.speed: Slow midrange / combo-loop — sets up through turns 2-4, takes over from turn 5 onward; wants the game to go long.
decks.strategy: Recursive value engine. Cheap green ramp and self-replacing fodder feed an aristocrat/recursion core; illusion tools (mirage, split, haunt) duplicate your best bodies at 1HP while Renewal/reclaim recycle the graveyard, so the deck never runs out of threats. It wins by making every death profitable and every removal a temporary inconvenience.
decks.hero: Гемма / Gemma — passive Facet: wake (awaken) any banked card in your mana row for its cost, and creatures woken this way enter with +1/+1. Lets you bank surplus bombs as crystals early, then redeploy them later as buffed bodies — bending ramp fuel back into threats and enabling off-curve captstones (Dormant Rampart, Dusk Hunter).
decks.matchups: MOST BEATS — Long Noon (Yellow control/lock): Yellow's blind/provoke/walls outlast fair decks, but Renewal+haunt+compost+reclaim produce an unkillable stream; the lock can disable one body, never the graveyard, and go-wide undergrowth floods past provoke walls while Second Sowing refills through their grind. You simply have more resources than they have answers. Bastion (Yellow/Green go-tall): Bastion commits to a few big bulwark/provoke bodies — Mirror Garden copies their giant or yours, undergrowth/go-wide outnumbers a small tall board, and Grove Skirmish + chump-and-recur trades down their key threats while you replace yours for free. MOST LOSES — Open Flame (Red aggro/tempo): the engine is a turn or two too slow; 1HP illusions, sprouts and 1/2 dorks evaporate to incandescence/pierce, and sear/spark reach the hero before Renewal snowballs — you only stabilize if you survive to T5, and Red doesn't allow it. Still Shroud (Yellow/Violet lock): blind+provoke+decoy strand your bodies, their refract shrugs off Grove Skirmish, and they grind on illusions too — the lock stops you converting card advantage into damage while their unmake picks off bombs before they can loop.

decks.speed: Slow control / lock. Stabilises by turn 4, sets the full prison by 5-6, then ticks to an inevitable kill.
decks.strategy: Prison-disable, not stall-outlast. Where Long Noon builds regenerating walls and waits, Still Shroud actively turns the enemy board OFF: provoke herds attackers onto sticky walls, blind/flare/warden strip their ability to act, refract+ward bounce their removal off our pieces. Once nothing on the far side can profitably attack or be answered, one untargetable/unblockable threat closes.
decks.wincon: A single locked-in evasive threat under a board the opponent cannot use: Silent Reaper (stealth+strobe, 8 unblockable/turn), Duskbound Matriarch (untargetable, ticking warden), a woken Buried Blade/Row Shade out of the mana row, or a Waking Colossus dropped mid-board that blinds everything on arrival. The lock makes any one of these lethal on a clock they can't race back.
decks.gameplan: T1: Dim Lamplighter blinds their 1-drop, or bank Row Shade / Buried Blade into the mana row as a hidden clock (decoy). T2: Light Shutter or Lantern Sentry — a provoke wall that soaks the first swings; or Blinding Glint their best attacker. T3: the herd-and-shut turn — Cage Keeper / Silent Ward provoke AND blind, Watch Beacon reads their banked cards, Long Dusk board-blinds a go-wide start. T4: engine online — Prison Warden makes blind tick every upkeep, Gaol Mirage forces attacks that then scatter (refract), Snuffing Verdict deletes anything you've already blinded. T5-6: the lock is sealed; deploy Silent Reaper or wake Waking Colossus (YYV) / a decoy'd threat, and let Duskbound Matriarch tick as an untargetable finisher. refract + ward keep the closer alive through their removal.
decks.curve_note: Control curve peaking at 3-4 (12 cards at 3, 10 at 4). Deliberately four 1-drops + eight 2-drops of blind/wall to survive the aggro matchups it is designed to lose; tops out at a single 6-drop capstone. Only two true 5+ finishers plus mana-row (decoy/awaken) threats that cost 0 to deploy when woken, so late flood is impossible.

decks.curve_note: Low tempo-forward curve, 1-6: 8/8/8/8/4/4 cards. Two of the four one-drops are ramp (Alluvium, Waterlily) and two are cheap interaction (Iceover, Ebbtide), so every opener does something. photosynthesis (Waterlily, Wellspring, Kingfisher) + add_crystal (Alluvium) pull the 5-6 payoffs out roughly a turn early; only two 6-drops as reachable tops. germinate bodies convert the crystal surplus into board width instead of dead mana. Mono-green ramp and mono-blue interaction are single-pip glue; every payoff/capstone is a heavy GG/GGB/GBB double-commit that only casts with hero fixing.
decks.gameplan: T1 (first): Alluvium (permanent crystal + scry) or Waterlily (0/3 ramp wall that also blocks a Red one-drop). T2: Wellspring / Mudskipper to develop and ramp, or hold Frost Minnow/Ice Jam to freeze their first real threat. By T3 you are on 4-5 crystals: drop a 4-cost body ahead of curve (Duckweed Raft bouncing a blocker, or Rapids freezing one) and start activating germinate to widen. T4-5: the double-green GGB payoffs come online while you still tempo them out — Quartz Newt is already a 6/6+ off your crystal count, Floodmother makes sprouts and bounces a blocker every turn, and Rime Sheet walls the ground while chilling their attack. T6: Floodlord freezes their whole board while you have a wide flooded field, or Spate Giant lands as an 11/14-class tank. Finish with Levee Break: three fresh sprouts + a board-wide +1/+1 turns an already-wide field into lethal, and it retroactively pumps every undergrowth/resonance body on the table. Throughout, freeze/scatter/chill mean the opponent never gets a clean profitable block, so your cheap ramped-up bodies chip 3-6 a turn from turn 3 onward.
decks.wincon: Wide flooded board of ramp-inflated cheap bodies that can't be blocked profitably, closed by Levee Break's sprout+board-buff alpha or Floodlord's freeze-all swing.
decks.hero: Ирида / Iris — Spectral Shift (spectral_shift): once per turn treat one of your crystals as an adjacent colour, fixing Green/Blue mana so the heavy GGB / GBB double-commit payoffs cast on time.
decks.matchups: MOST BEATS — Overgrowth (Green ramp-bombs): Floodtide is the faster, wider clock; freeze + scatter neutralize their one-at-a-time bombs (bounce a resolved bomb, freeze the next) while a flooded board races them before they stabilize. Bastion (Yellow/Green go-tall): a handful of tall provoke/wall blockers can't cover a go-wide board; scatter resets their growth/shield investment and freeze turns off their one big attacker, so you flank and race. MOST LOSES — Open Flame (Red aggro): the ramp/setup plan is a turn too slow; bypass/pierce ignore your blockers and burn reach closes before the flood matures, and Waterlily/Rime Sheet only buy so much. Glass Hour (Blue control/spells): they out-freeze and out-scatter you, chill/haze blunt the wide board, and their card-advantage + sweep-style answers grind go-wide into the ground — your payoffs are individually fragile to their superior tempo tools.

decks.gameplan: Ход 1-3: разложить стену с provoke (Портик, Барбакан, Живая изгородь) и включить рамп (Подсолнух, Кристальный сад). Алебардщик с firststrike меняется 1-в-1 с ранними атакерами; Bulwark с Барбакана/Ясного дня начинает капать броню на героя, mulch (Дернина/Ясный день) и cauterize чинят просадку. Ход 4-5: стены множатся, provoke стягивает весь урон на неубиваемые тела, а рамп уже на 6-7 кристаллах. Приземляем первый растущий тайтан — Небесная твердь или Молодой дуб — и он проходит порог 6 HP, включая пассивку Атланта. Ход 6-8: выкатываем капстоун (Атлантов дуб / Кряжистый вяз / Донжон), страхуем его Покровом (ward+shield) от единственного, что нас убивает — таргет-снятия. Под бронёй, стенами, regen и пассивкой это тело нельзя убрать; growth/undergrowth раздувают его до 12/12+, strobe бьёт дважды и закрывает игру за 1-2 хода. Затмение придерживает вражескую бомбу, пока тайтан добивает.
decks.wincon: Один неубиваемый go-tall тайтан. Атлантов дуб / Кряжистый вяз / Донжон под провокой стен, бронёй Bulwark, regen и пассивкой Атланта дорастает growth/undergrowth до 12/12+ и закрывает игру за 1-2 удара через strobe (двойная атака). Это не капающий дрейн аутласта, а разовый финиш телом.

engine_work: NEW trigger event Healed (on_heal): wrap the single heal-resolution path (hero-heal + creature-heal) so each heal instance fires reactTo on the healed side's board -> Reflux N -> dealHeroDamage. A heal-all resolves one event per healed entity. GUARD: Reflux/Requiem damage must not itself heal (no loop). Consumers: Reflux (LN, RG), and it chains off Dawnlight, loam, cauterize, regen, Stained Glass, Lull/Total Eclipse.

NEW trigger event SpellCast (on_spell_cast): in playCard, after a type==Spell resolves, fire reactTo over the caster's board and maintain a spellsCastThisTurn counter reset at turn start. Consumers: the prowess keyword and chain_burn. Add EventType entries (current enum is only TurnStart/TurnEnd/Summoned/Died/DamageDealt).

RENAME CONFLICT: the decks' echo/Отклик (prowess, +N/+0 per spell) collides with the engine's EXISTING keyword literally named echo (Penta Prism aura, first spell of the turn resolves twice, game.cpp:390-402). Give the new prowess keyword a distinct internal id (e.g. prowess) and leave engine echo untouched; card text can keep 'Отклик'.

NEW keywords, register + resolve: Reflux N (on_heal payoff), Requiem N (friendly-death: dealHeroDamage(enemy,N)+heal(owner,N)), Bulwark N (start_of_turn hero +N armor via existing heroArmor field/absorb path), harvest N (activated: sacrifice another friendly then +N/+N, once/turn, target!=self), warden N (start_of_turn: blind N random un-blinded enemies, reuse blind counter), prowess N (on_spell_cast temp +N/+0).

NEW graveyard recursion Renewal N (on_death) + reclaim action: move N random creature cards from owner's graveyard (already tracked, but game.hpp:148 notes nothing reads it yet) to hand, respecting hand-cap 10 (overflow stays). Same underlying op exposed as executeAction 'reclaim' with value. Consumers: Overgrowth (Everbloom), RG (Sprouting Corpse), Evergreen (Barrow Ivy, Second Sowing=reclaim 2).

NEW action fight(source,target): two-target spell shape (chosen_friendly_minion + chosen_enemy_minion) — extend the effect/target resolver to accept a second selector for one spell — then mutual dealDamage in one batch and run Died checks/on_death for both. Consumers: Overgrowth (Strangleveil), Evergreen (Grove Skirmish), Floodtide.

NEW action sacrifice: move a chosen friendly (not self) to graveyard, firing on_death and all friendly-death reactions (spores/haunt/loam/Requiem/compost). Single-target (harvest, Sacrificial Sheaf) and multi-target 0..n selector (Wake). Wake then does 2*count to enemy hero after each body's on_death chain resolves.

matchup_table:
Consistency check first: every pair where BOTH decks named the matchup AGREES on the winner — zero contradictions (no two decks both claim to beat each other). That is the single healthiest sign. Grid below is one-line per deck (specified matchups only; ~25 of 55 pairs were left unstated by both authors and are OPEN).

Open Flame (R aggro): BEATS Overgrowth, Glass Hour, Floodtide, Evergreen, Still Shroud | LOSES Long Noon, Rot and Bloom, Bastion | ~5-3, field-best. The metagame's reference clock.
Long Noon (Y wall-control): BEATS Open Flame, False Light | LOSES Overgrowth, Arc Light, Evergreen | ~2-3.
Overgrowth (G ramp): BEATS Long Noon, Glass Hour, Rot and Bloom, Bastion | LOSES Open Flame, Arc Light, Still Shroud, Floodtide | ~4-4 even.
Glass Hour (B control): BEATS False Light, Arc Light, Rot and Bloom, Floodtide | LOSES Open Flame, Overgrowth, Bastion | ~4-3.
False Light (V swarm): BEATS Bastion, Rot and Bloom | LOSES Glass Hour, Long Noon | ~2-2 (many open).
Rot and Bloom (RG aristocrats): BEATS Open Flame, Still Shroud | LOSES Glass Hour, False Light, Overgrowth | ~2-3.
Arc Light (RB combo-aggro): BEATS Long Noon, Overgrowth | LOSES Glass Hour, Bastion | ~2-2.
Evergreen (GV recursion): BEATS Long Noon, Bastion | LOSES Open Flame, Still Shroud | ~2-2.
Still Shroud (YV lock): BEATS Overgrowth, Evergreen | LOSES Open Flame, Rot and Bloom | ~2-2.
Floodtide (GB tempo): BEATS Overgrowth, Bastion | LOSES Open Flame, Glass Hour | ~2-2.
Bastion (YG go-tall): BEATS Open Flame, Arc Light, Glass Hour | LOSES Overgrowth, False Light, Floodtide, Evergreen | ~3-4.

The RPS spine: aggro (Open Flame / Arc Light) > greedy ramp & durdle control (Overgrowth, Glass Hour, Floodtide) > anti-aggro walls (Long Noon, Bastion, Rot and Bloom) > and combo/lock (Evergreen, Still Shroud, False Light) cut sideways across it. Removal-light go-tall/one-bomb plans (Bastion, Overgrowth's single capstone) are correctly preyed on by unmake/bounce/lock (False Light, Floodtide, Still Shroud).

VERDICT: healthy competitive web, NOT broken. No dead deck (every deck beats >=2 others) and no dominant deck (every deck loses to >=2, Open Flame to 3). Concerns, honestly: (1) Open Flame is the clear ceiling (5-3) and the whole field is balanced around hating it — if aggro gets underplayed the three dedicated aggro-hate decks (Long Noon, Bastion, Rot and Bloom, all sub-.500) lose their prey and become free wins for midrange/combo. Only 2 of 11 decks are true aggro to feed 3 aggro-haters — a lopsided predator/prey ratio. (2) Overgrowth is a hub: it beats 3 control/midrange decks and only folds to speed/disruption; watch it doesn't become the 'greedy default.' (3) ~45% of the grid is unmapped, so this verdict covers the stated cells only.
